raw.details:
Overview

Innovate. Build. Break Barriers.

About the Hackathon

ISTE TCET invites passionate innovators, developers, designers, and problem-solvers to participate in an exciting hackathon that challenges participants to transform ideas into impactful solutions.

The hackathon provides a platform for students to collaborate, think creatively, explore emerging technologies, and develop innovative solutions to real-world problems. Whether you are a coder, designer, researcher, or aspiring entrepreneur, this is your opportunity to showcase your skills, experiment with technology, and bring your ideas to life.

Work in teams, tackle challenging problem statements, build functional prototypes, and compete with fellow innovators. Push your limits, learn from the experience, and turn your imagination into innovation!

Domains

Participants can explore innovative solutions across the following domains:

  • Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI/ML): Intelligent systems, predictive analytics, automation, generative AI, and AI-powered applications.
  • Web Development: Innovative websites, web applications, SaaS platforms, and digital solutions.
  • Mobile Application Development: Android/iOS applications, cross-platform solutions, and mobile-first innovations.
  • Blockchain & Web3: Decentralized applications, smart contracts, digital identity, and secure transactions.
  • Cybersecurity: Network security, threat detection, data privacy, and secure digital infrastructure.
  • Internet of Things (IoT): Smart devices, automation, connected systems, and sensor-based solutions.
  • Healthcare & MedTech: Healthcare accessibility, patient management, medical innovation, and wellness solutions.
  • FinTech: Digital payments, financial inclusion, banking solutions, and financial automation.
  • Sustainability & Smart Cities: Environmental solutions, waste management, energy efficiency, and smart infrastructure.
  • Open Innovation: Any technology-driven solution addressing a meaningful real-world problem.

Participation Guidelines

  • Participation is open to eligible college students.
  • Participants must register within the specified registration deadline.
  • Teams may consist of 2–4 members.
  • Interdisciplinary teams are encouraged.
  • Each team must nominate one team leader as the primary point of contact.
  • All team members must be registered successfully.

Hackathon Rules & Regulations

  • All projects must be developed during the designated hackathon period.
  • Pre-existing projects cannot be submitted as original hackathon solutions. However, previously developed libraries, frameworks, and open-source tools may be used.
  • Teams must develop solutions relevant to the selected domain or assigned problem statement.
  • Plagiarism, duplication, and misrepresentation of work will result in disqualification.
  • Teams must submit their source code, project documentation, and working prototype within the stipulated deadline.
  • Participants must ensure that their projects are functional and demonstrable during evaluation.
  • Any use of AI tools, APIs, third-party libraries, and open-source resources must be appropriately acknowledged.
  • Teams must maintain professional conduct throughout the event.
  • The decision of the judging panel and organizing committee will be final.
  • Organizers reserve the right to modify the event schedule, rules, or guidelines when necessary.
  • Evaluation Criteria

Projects will be evaluated based on the following parameters:

  • Innovation & Originality: 20%
  • Technical Implementation: 25%
  • Problem Relevance & Impact: 20%
  • Functionality & Execution: 20%
  • Presentation & Pitch: 15%

Project Submission Requirements

Each team must submit:

  • Project title and selected domain.
  • Problem statement and proposed solution.
  • Working prototype or Minimum Viable Product (MVP).
  • Source code repository (GitHub or equivalent).
  • Project presentation (PPT).
  • Brief documentation explaining the implementation, technology stack, and future scope.
  • Demonstration of the working solution.

What to Expect

  • An opportunity to transform ideas into real-world solutions.
  • Hands-on experience with emerging technologies.
  • Networking and collaboration with fellow innovators.
  • Expert evaluation and feedback.
  • Recognition, certificates, and exciting prizes for outstanding teams.

Important Note

Participants are expected to bring their own laptops and any additional hardware required for their projects. Further information regarding the venue, schedule, problem statements, submission deadlines, and other event-specific instructions will be communicated by the organizing committee.

Organized by ISTE TCET

Think Beyond. Build Beyond. Innovate Beyond.
